content.comment_body: I attempted to run an online test, but received a message stating that online testing isn't possible because the circuit programs on the device and the PC software don't match. I uploaded the program from the controller to the computer from scratch and tried the online test again. After this error, I used the comparison tool, and it indicated that there were no differences between the controller and the program uploaded to my computer. I repeated this process multiple times but the problem persisted. What could be causing this? My setup includes: [company_name] [product_name] ([article_no]), [product_name] [version_no], connected via Ethernet cable.

The parameters of the blocks may have changed while the program was running. [product_name] checks the parameters of the offline program and compares them to those of the online program before allowing online testing.
If block parameters change during runtime, how can I figure out which parameters have changed and what values need to be adjusted on my PC to enable online testing?

It's unusual that the comparison tool doesn't show any differences in your case. Make sure to check at the bottom of the software page, where the version of the [product_name] is listed. It is important to specify the correct version. I've had issues where some things seemed to work despite a mismatch, but other aspects didn't function properly.
The message clearly says: You should use the online program downloaded from [product_name] and compare it with the offline program.

I'm confused about what I'm doing wrong. I go to tools > compare, connect to the controller, the process stops the controller to get the diagram, and afterwards the diagrams compared are identical. How do I get the specific online version? The comparison tool requires me to stop the controller. What steps am I missing?
Did you press the Start button?
Yes, I did. Additionally, the program exported from the controller opens in the 'Network Project' tab, not in the 'Diagram mode' tab.
It doesn't matter if a program is loaded onto the [product_name] in network or diagram mode. Can you upload your program as a ZIP file?
Can you also upload the online version of the program?
That's exactly the issue—I can't export the online program to my computer! When I try, it appears to be the same as before.

That's odd. You're unable to download the program from the [product_name] to your PC? Is there any error message? Please specify: What exact [product_name] model do you have? State the full order number and firmware version. Which [product_name] software version is installed?

We discovered a mistake in the diagram, downloaded the corrected program to the controller, and then the online test worked. The issue was with the program present on the controller initially, so online testing not working wasn't due to the previous steps.
What was the specific mistake? Also, why was it not possible to download the program from the [product_name] to the PC?

We were able to upload from controller to PC, but the online testing tool kept telling us the diagrams weren't identical, which was confusing since the program was just uploaded from the same controller.
I'm sorry, but I still find this unclear.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience confusion when trying to conduct online testing with [product_name] [version_no] and a [product_name] device. A persistent error message about circuit program mismatches appears, even though comparison tools show no differences. Users are unsure about block parameter changes during runtime and the distinction between online and offline program states, making it hard to identify what the software considers 'identical'. The lack of clear instructions and workflow explanation leads to a challenging troubleshooting process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to accurately identify when programs on the controller and PC are identical, easily highlight any discrepancies including parameter changes, and provide a straightforward online testing process without repeated errors or ambiguous feedback.
